facts.statement: The genus Lingyuanosaurus was formally described and named in 2019 by a team including Xi Yao, Chun-Chi Liao, Corwin Sullivan, and Xu Xing.
facts.quote: Lingyuanosaurus was formally described and named in 2019 in a publication authored by Xi Yao, Chun-Chi Liao, Corwin Sullivan, and Xu Xing.

facts.statement: The generic name Lingyuanosaurus honors the city of Lingyuan and the Ancient Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name, Lingyuanosaurus, is in reference to county-level city of Lingyuan, and the Ancient Greek word saûros (σαῦρος), Latinized as saurus, meaning "lizard".

facts.statement: The specific name sihedangensis refers to the town of Sihedang where the fossil was found.
facts.quote: The specific name, sihedangensis, is in reference to its place of discovery as well, the town of Sihedang.

facts.statement: Lingyuanosaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous period in Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: Lingyuanosaurus is a genus of therizinosaurian theropod from the Early Cretaceous of Liaoning Province, China.

facts.statement: The environment where Lingyuanosaurus lived had an average yearly temperature of 10°C, featuring relatively cold winters.
facts.quote: The average yearly temperature during the time of Lingyuanosaurus was 10 C, with relatively cold winters for the generally warm Mesozoic era.

facts.statement: Lingyuanosaurus was a small therizinosaur approximately 2.2 meters long.
facts.quote: Lingyuanosaurus was a relatively small therizinosaurian, similar in size to the closely related Beipiaosaurus at about 2.2 m long.

facts.statement: Based on a femur length of 200 mm, researchers estimated the weight of Lingyuanosaurus to be about 12 kg.
facts.quote: The femur of the specimen was only 200 mm long, and Yao and colleagues used its circumference to estimate a weight of about 12 kg.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Lingyuanosaurus includes various postcranial bones such as vertebrae, ribs, partial arm and leg bones, and claws.
facts.quote: The holotype, and only specimen, IVPP V 23589 consists of several bones of the postcranial skeleton including the vertebral centrum of a cervical vertebra, five partial vertebrae (dorsals, sacrals, and caudals), a single complete caudal vertebrae, several ribs from the middle and lower back, the proximal half of the right humerus, the distal half of the left humerus, two manual unguals, a mostly complete ilium, part of an ischium, the right femur, part of the left tibia, part of the right astragalus, and several pieces of bone that could not be identified.

facts.statement: Lingyuanosaurus is distinguished from other therizinosaurs by specific traits including a plate on dorsal vertebrae, unique vertebrae articulations, and a distinctively shaped ilium.
facts.quote: Lingyuanosaurus can be distinguished from all other therizinosaurs by the following combination of traits: a lamina (or "plate") present on the dorsal vertebrae separating the two infradiapophyseal fossae, unique anatomy of the hyposphene-hypantrum articulation, and an ilium with a strongly convex upper edge and a concave lower edge, and the presence of a roughly triangle-shaped fossa just above the pubic peduncle.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the Lingyuanosaurus specimen died before reaching full maturity.
facts.quote: In their description of Lingyuanosaurus, Yao and colleagues suggested that the specimen was probably not fully-grown when it died.

facts.statement: Lingyuanosaurus possesses a proximodorsal lip on its claws, a feature found in basal therizinosaur taxa.
facts.quote: However, this "proximodorsal lip" is present in basal therizinosaur taxa such as Lingyuanosaurus and Falcarius.

facts.statement: While the presence of a proximodorsal lip suggests claws could be used for feeding or digging, specific functions for Lingyuanosaurus claws remain unproposed.
facts.quote: This may have permitted the claws of these taxa to be used to assist in feeding, digging, or locomotion, although the authors do not suggest any such specific uses for the claws in Lingyuanosaurus.

facts.statement: The dietary habits of Lingyuanosaurus are unknown because no skull remains have been found.
facts.quote: No remains of the skull of Lingyuanosaurus are known, so the dietary habits of the animal are not directly known.

facts.statement: It is possible that Lingyuanosaurus was herbivorous, as most known therizinosaurs were.
facts.quote: However, most known therizinosaurs are believed to have been herbivorous, so it is possible that Lingyuanosaurus was as well.

facts.statement: Despite only 45 out of over 300 character states being assignable due to incompleteness, analysis confirmed Lingyuanosaurus belongs to Therizinosauria.
facts.quote: Because of its incompleteness, they were only able to assign 45 character states to Lingyuanosaurus (out of a total of over 300), however their results using multiple methodologies and datasets confirmed the genus' place within Therizinosauria.

facts.statement: Lingyuanosaurus is considered to represent an evolutionary transition within the therizinosaur lineage.
facts.quote: Lingyuanosaurus is believed to represent an evolutionary transition within therizinosaurs.

facts.statement: The paleoenvironment of the Jehol Group, where Lingyuanosaurus lived, featured warm and humid conditions with seasonal dry periods.
facts.quote: Studies suggest that the paleoenvironment of the Jehol Group involved seasonal climate fluctuations, and was warm and humid, punctuated by dry seasons, in which the environment became more arid.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Lingyuanosaurus was discovered near the town of Sihedang.
facts.quote: The holotype of Lingyuanosaurus, given the designation IVPP V 23589, was discovered at a fossil locality near a town called Sihedang.

facts.statement: Lingyuanosaurus fossils were found within the Jehol biota, though the exact geological formation and precise age remain unknown.
facts.quote: It was uncovered within one of the formations that make up the Jehol biota, although the exact geological formation — and therefore also its precise geological age — is unknown.

facts.statement: The genus Lingyuanosaurus was described by Yao and colleagues in 2019.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Yao et al., 2019

facts.statement: The only known species of the genus is L. sihedangensis.
facts.quote: species: L. sihedangensis

facts.statement: Lingyuanosaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, between 133 and 120 million years ago, from the Barremian to the Aptian.
facts.quote: vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, entre 133 a 120 millones de años, desde el Barremiense al Aptiense

facts.statement: Fossils of Lingyuanosaurus have been found in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy Asia

facts.statement: The species L. sihedangensis is known from fossils found within a layer of the Jehol Group.
facts.quote: Solo se conoce a una especie, L. sihedangensis encontrado dentro de una capa del Grupo Jehol.

facts.statement: The original describers classified Lingyuanosaurus as a basal therizinosaur.
facts.quote: Aunque para los descriptores fue un tericinosaurio basal

facts.statement: Researcher Mickey Mortimer suggests that Lingyuanosaurus might have been an oviraptorosaur instead of a therizinosaur.
facts.quote: según Mickey Mortimer, Lingyuanosaurus pudo haber sido un oviraptorosaurio.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists Therizinosauria as the parent group for Lingyuanosaurus.
facts.quote: Parent group: Therizinosauria

facts.statement: The time range for Lingyuanosaurus is recorded as the Aptian, from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
